varieties.name: 1000 Headed (Chou Moellier / Thousand Headed)
varieties.season: Spring to autumn (per Kirchhoffs); Starke Ayres markets it as an all-year full-sun crop
varieties.traits: Highly productive, tender leaves; "does not handle extreme heat" per Kirchhoffs' page for the same Thousand Headed type
varieties.note: This is the same variety crop-catalog.ts's own inline comments already rely on for kale's sow-window and 55-120 day maturity range (Starke Ayres 1000 Headed/Black Tuscan pages + Kirchhoffs Chou Moullier Thousand Headed page); this file adds it as an actual CropVariety entry, which the catalog did not previously have for kale. Its heat intolerance (already noted in the catalog's own farmer-facing note) is the real reason to favour it in the cooler zones (highveld, midlands-mistbelt, high-mountain) and sow it only in cooler months in the hot zones (lowveld-bushveld, karoo-arid, subtropical-coast).

evidence.quote: 1000 Headed Kale is a highly productive variety with tender, nutrient-packed leaves. It's perfect for fresh eating, smoothies, and cooking.
evidence.doc: 1000 Headed Kale, Starke Ayres product page (via search snippet — JS-rendered page, not directly fetchable for a verbatim on-page quote)

varieties.name: Black Tuscan (Lacinato / Dinosaur kale)
varieties.season: Sold alongside 1000 Headed as an all-year Starke Ayres offering
varieties.traits: Deep green, highly nutritious, rich flavour leaves — the narrow-leaf Italian type, distinct from the broad-leaf 1000 Headed
varieties.note: A second nationally-marketed kale type, offering a leaf-shape/texture alternative to 1000 Headed for salads specifically.

evidence.quote: Black Tuscan Kale, also known as Lacinato or Dinosaur Kale, offers deep green, highly nutritious leaves with a rich flavor. It's perfect for salads and cooking.
evidence.doc: Black Tuscan Kale, Starke Ayres product page (via search snippet — JS-rendered page, not directly fetchable for a verbatim on-page quote)

lowveld-bushveld.text: No source states kale is unsuited here, but crop-catalog.ts's own note (carried over, not re-verified in this pass) says kale 'does not handle extreme heat', and this is the hottest of the 8 zones — treat both varieties as a cool-season-only planting here, not a year-round one.

karoo-arid.text: Same heat caveat as lowveld-bushveld applies to Karoo summers; no zone-specific kale source was found for the Karoo.

gaps: Both varieties are marketed nationally with no explicit zone restriction; the zone lists above are the full 8-zone set with a heat caveat noted in zoneAdvice, not a per-zone sourced recommendation.

As with green-beans and swiss-chard, the Starke Ayres product pages are JS-rendered and could not be independently fetched for verbatim on-page text in this pass — quotes come from a WebSearch summary of that page, flagged rather than hidden.

The Kirchhoffs Chou Moullier Thousand Headed page that crop-catalog.ts's own comments cite (for the 40x40cm spacing, 1cm/2mm depth and heat-intolerance note) was not re-opened in this pass; it is carried over as the existing catalog's basis, not independently re-verified here.
